title: Setup: The Three Formulations of Firoozbakht's Conjecture
content: The header lays out Firoozbakht's 1982 conjecture in its three interchangeable forms: the original ROOT form (p_n^{1/n} strictly decreasing), the RPOW form p_{n+1} < p_n^{1+1/n}, and the INTEGER-POWER form p_{n+1}^n < p_n^{n+1}. It stresses the central distinction: the conjecture is open (verified past 10^19), but the EQUIVALENCE of its three formulations is an unconditional theorem. The gallery's BoundedPrimeGaps.lean formalizes only the RPOW form; this file supplies the bridges to the other two. The file imports only Mathlib and is axiom-free.
mathContext: With $p_n$ the $n$-th prime, the three statements for $n \ge 1$ are: ROOT $p_{n+1}^{1/(n+1)} < p_n^{1/n}$; RPOW $p_{n+1} < p_n^{1+1/n}$; INTPOW $p_{n+1}^n < p_n^{n+1}$. The last is a statement purely in $\mathbb{N}$.

title: root_lt_iff: Root Form ⟺ Core Inequality
content: For positive reals a, b and n ≥ 1, root_lt_iff proves a^{1/(n+1)} < b^{1/n} ⟺ a^n < b^{n+1} (all real rpow). The proof raises both sides to the positive power n(n+1) via Real.rpow_lt_rpow_iff (strict monotonicity of x ↦ x^c for c > 0 on nonnegatives), then collapses the nested exponents with Real.rpow_mul: the left exponent 1/(n+1) · n(n+1) simplifies to n, the right 1/n · n(n+1) to n+1, each discharged by field_simp. The resulting iff is the core, taken symm.
mathContext: Because $x \mapsto x^{n(n+1)}$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, applying it to both sides is an equivalence. $\big(a^{1/(n+1)}\big)^{n(n+1)} = a^{n}$ and $\big(b^{1/n}\big)^{n(n+1)} = b^{n+1}$.

title: rpow_lt_iff: Rpow Form ⟺ Core Inequality
content: For positive reals a, b and n ≥ 1, rpow_lt_iff proves a < b^{1+1/n} ⟺ a^n < b^{n+1} (real rpow). The proof raises both sides to the power n via Real.rpow_lt_rpow_iff; the right side b^{(1+1/n)·n} collapses to b^{n+1} by Real.rpow_mul and field_simp, while the left stays a^n. This is the gallery's RPOW form reduced to the same core as root_lt_iff.
mathContext: $x \mapsto x^{n}$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, so $a < b^{1+1/n} \iff a^{n} < \big(b^{1+1/n}\big)^{n} = b^{n+1}$ since $(1+1/n)\cdot n = n+1$.

title: core_real_iff_nat: Real Core ⟺ Natural-Number Inequality
content: core_real_iff_nat shows the real-rpow core (p:ℝ)^n < (q:ℝ)^{n+1} is equivalent to the natural-number inequality p^n < q^{n+1} for p, q : ℕ. Since both exponents are natural, Real.rpow_natCast turns the real powers into monoid powers, ← Nat.cast_pow pulls the casts outward, and Nat.cast_lt reflects the strict inequality from ℝ down to ℕ. This is the bridge that makes the integer-power form an honest ℕ-statement.
mathContext: For naturals, $(p:\mathbb{R})^{(n:\mathbb{R})} = ((p^n : \mathbb{N}):\mathbb{R})$ and the cast $\mathbb{N} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a strict-order embedding, so the real and natural inequalities coincide.

title: The Prime Sequence and the Three Prime Formulations
content: nthPrime n = Nat.nth Nat.Prime n (so p_0 = 2, p_1 = 3, …, matching the gallery convention), with nthPrime_pos giving positivity from Nat.prime_nth_prime. The three formulations are then stated for primes: FiroozbakhtRoot (root form, the original 1982 statement), FiroozbakhtRpow (definitionally the gallery's FireoozbakhtConjecture), and FiroozbakhtIntPow (the integer-power form, a Prop purely about ℕ).
mathContext: $\texttt{nthPrime}$ indexes primes from $0$. Each formulation quantifies over $n \ge 1$; the $n \ge 1$ hypothesis is needed because the exponents $1/n$ and $1/(n+1)$ require $n > 0$.

title: The Three Formulations Are Equivalent (TFAE)
content: firoozbakht_root_iff_intPow and firoozbakht_rpow_iff_intPow chain the pointwise lemmas (root_lt_iff / rpow_lt_iff) with core_real_iff_nat, using nthPrime_pos for the positivity hypotheses; firoozbakht_root_iff_rpow follows by transitivity. firoozbakht_forms_tfae packages all three as a List.TFAE via tfae_have 1↔3, tfae_have 2↔3, tfae_finish. The result is unconditional: it states only that the three formulations coincide, not that any of them holds.
mathContext: Each prime formulation is the pointwise equivalence applied at $a = p_{n+1}$, $b = p_n$, composed with the real-to-nat bridge. $\text{ROOT} \iff \text{INTPOW} \iff \text{RPOW}$, hence all three are equivalent.
